ending_false.text: (You close the notebook. For a moment your thumb rests in the seam between the black and the white.)
(You have the odd feeling that you have been to this city before. This is like all the cities that you've encountered before. Nothing less. Nothing more.)
(You picked up Aurora's call.)

ending_false.speaker: Aurora
ending_false.text: I have it. Thank you. You must be tired.

ending_false.speaker: Aurora
ending_false.text: Can I ask you something before you go? Did anyone ever come back to the cemetery?

ending_false.speaker: #PLAYER#
ending_false.text: There were traces of visitors. I couldn’t tell you who they came for.

ending_false.speaker: Aurora
ending_false.text: I see. And did you find anything on your way out?

ending_false.speaker: #PLAYER#
ending_false.text: Just the way back.
(She gives a little laugh. You recognize the sound. She made it the first time you told her you’d landed safely.)

ending_false.speaker: Aurora
ending_false.text: Of course. Have a safe journey home.
(You wait for her to say she’ll speak to you again. The radio clicks. You put it away.)
(You walk the same way you came. Your footprints are still there. You find it reassuring that there is something here you can recognize at a glance.)
(A few steps later, you hear her question again. Did you find anything? There was a small lift in her voice on the last word. You had mistaken it for the courtesy of someone letting you finish.)
(You recognize that sound now. Someone has spent a long time imagining the answer. You wonder what she had hoped you would say.)
(Perhaps there were stories you passed close enough to touch. Every day people pass that close to you. They go home, turn on a light, and forget they ever saw you. You have done the same to them.)
(There was a first morning on this planet, and there was a last one anyone woke up to see. For a little while, between those mornings, people knew who they were waiting for.)
(At the ship, you find yourself trying to remember a stone from the planet. It is strange that you miss something that doesn't really relate to your life.)
(Tomorrow the sun will rise. You start to think whether you left any coffee in your cup before you left. You hope there is no flies landing in it, or worse, hope it doesn’t stink.)

(For a while the radio could still reach her. You leave it beside you and watch the Twins recede. First time you really see the planet from far, in a nicely divided black and white. You are in awe of that spectacular scene.)

(Years from now, you may remember that you once knew someone named Aurora. You may even remember that she was waiting for something, but that's it. By then, the world she carried will have slipped as far into your memory as it now slips into the dark, wild universe.)

query_night_ascending_path.speaker: Aurora
query_night_ascending_path.text: A path leading upward, toward the surface. It records a journey. It does not tell us how steep the path was or why the traveller died.

query_night_crystal_god.speaker: Aurora
query_night_crystal_god.text: The Crystal God. It marks faith in the deity, and the Nightfolk also leave it on graves as a blessing for the departed. The same figure can appear on an altar or a personal memorial; its presence alone does not tell us who removed the crystals.

query_night_dry_river.speaker: Aurora
query_night_dry_river.text: It represents a river that has run dry. That is the meaning of the symbol. Whether it describes this place, a loss of water, or the circumstances of her death needs further evidence.

query_night_unending_path.speaker: Aurora
query_night_unending_path.text: That is it. “A journey without end”: the blessing and this path say the same thing. Someone left and did not return, and the Nightfolk call that <link="disappearance">disappearance</link>.

query_night_unending_path.speaker: Aurora
query_night_unending_path.text: It does not tell us what happened to that person.

query_night_unending_path_hint.speaker: Aurora
query_night_unending_path_hint.text: A path that does not end and does not return.

query_night_unending_path_hint.speaker: Aurora
query_night_unending_path_hint.text: I have heard that idea before, in one of the translations I gave you: a journey without end. Look back through my words, and bring me the one that says it.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Day City records a death. Night City records a <link="disappearance">disappearance</link>. That difference does not mean there were two children. Check the figures together.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Compare the figures first, then we'll see.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Not everything can be interpreted with a modern mindset, and not all offerings are intended for commercial exchange. These are blessings given by the Nightfolk.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Show me the stones first.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The Crystal God stood there intact. The crystals were later pried out. Day City needed crystal, but I cannot prove they did it. For now, you can take this as a provisional argument.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Use the searchlight on the empty recess. We need to see what was there.

test_answer_altar_24.text: (The silence lasts just a fraction longer than the question seems to need. Her reply is direct.)

test_answer_altar_24.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_altar_24.text: A symbol can be remembered without a written language. Someone who used it could pass on its meaning. I am not working from books alone.

test_answer_altar_28.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_altar_28.text: Check the division first. If it was wrong, 'born in the wrong city' may be the wrong question. Keep the two memorials together.
(Her voice stops abruptly. The night spills around you, with barely a sound. You start to think about how the Day City looked, and your call with Aurora then.)
(It's different, definitely. Two worlds overlap in the dimension of time.)
(Was it "wrong"? Or is it just a glimpse through the overlap?)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: It is the Crystal God, the Nightfolk's sign of faith. Left on a grave, it is also a blessing: “To disappear is to set out on a journey without end. May the wishes of crystal remain with you.” It wishes the departed well.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Photograph the same sign on all three graves first. Bring me that record, and I can read it for you.

test_answer_altar_crystal_shape.text: (You look from the carving to the crystal in the scene. The outline is the same, and for a moment the sign seems less carved than set down.)

test_answer_altar_crystal_shape.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_altar_crystal_shape.text: Set the stone beside the carving: the same facets, the same point at the top. The Nightfolk did not picture their god as a person. They carved the crystal itself.

test_answer_altar_crystal_shape.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_altar_crystal_shape.text: It is what they dug from the dark and came to trust. A figure made of that stone is faith, and it is also a blessing: “May the wishes of crystal remain with you.”

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Before we ask why, perhaps we should ask why not. Day City remembers a life through its work. This <link="infant">child</link> was the first to die without an identifiable occupation. So the designer gave him something no title was needed for: the shape of a person.

("A child without an occupation is a person before anything else,” you were reminded of the quote from the manuscript. Despite the punchline, or slogan that speaks to everyone else but the infant, can he really separate from the social influence?)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Yes, this is an icon for the Dayfolk. Have you found a designer's manuscript that explains why this marker was shaped like a person?

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Compare the rubbing with the figure in the cemetery. What do the two shapes have in common?

test_answer_baby_21.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_baby_21.text: I cannot tell you who drew it, #PLAYER#. Perhaps someone had grown tired of seeing the same approved face carved over every life that did not fit.
(She seems to have personal feelings about this topic.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Yes, it does look like a moon. I suppose sleep is the closest rehearsal the living have for death. When night falls, the Dayfolk slip into slumber. On this marker, the moon stands for <link="natural">natural death</link>.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The outline is a starting point. Show me your comparison with the moon, and we can ask what it meant to the Dayfolk.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The moon offers a peaceful ending, but that is the story the family chose to put in stone. If the child's real face was left out, perhaps there were <link="unexplained death">unexplained circumstances</link> behind his death. Let us keep looking.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The path was uneven, but it was not a dangerous climb. He kept searching <link="missed_sleeping_deadline">beyond the permitted waking hours</link> and failed to reach a sleeping coffin in time.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Check the actual path or its history. An upward line does not show how steep it was.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: One dies. The other disappears at dawn. Check whether these are two records of one life.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Bring the Scholar's <link="disappearance">disappearance</link> report. We need the time her husband vanished.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: It is a blessing for the person who left. Nobody was paying for the path.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Record the stone. Compare it with the altar offerings.

test_answer_father_24.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_father_24.text: The history calls it natural. Shared coffins weaken the claim that there was no room. They do not prove who caused the collapse. We need separate evidence for that.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The same child. Look at the way he is held. The man carrying him is his <link="night_father">father in Night City</link>.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Match the child with the altar figure before you name the parent.
(For a moment, the sentence seems to cost her more than it should.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The diary writer carved memorials and came to question the stories they were asked to preserve. She was a <link="funerary_artist">funerary artist</link>. Perhaps this was the one stone she could finally let speak for herself.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: A human shape can stand for many lives. Her work may have left a clearer signature in the diary.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The four figures match the family photograph. Three markers share a base; the girl’s marker stands apart. The sculpture and photograph let us identify the same family across the two sites.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Let us put the four little figures beside the four faces. We should know the family before we name its missing place.
(She draws out the first word, then presses the rest into an even rhythm. You hear how much work the evenness takes.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The diary gives the two girls different reasons to leave. One could no longer bear what her mother defended. The other had spent years waiting to be noticed, first beside her brother, then beside the space he left. Their departure was deliberate. A memorial can mark an absence without proving a death.
(The silence feels less like thought than resistance. You wait until it gives way.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Read what she meant to do. A stone can remember an absence without knowing where the person went.

test_answer_girl_24.text: You are about to ask Aurora about the girl on the cover. Are you ready to begin the final conversation?

items.label: Begin the final conversation.
Keep investigating.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: An upright sleeping coffin, just like the old illustration. A change in how people slept can leave a surprisingly long shadow.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: That frame has an older history than the girl inside it. Let us look for its shape in the book.
(You almost asked that question, but deep down, you know why it’s here.)
(You decided not to ask this way.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Anything else?

else.speaker: Aurora
else.text: I'm not sure what you are talking about.

then.text: (If your guess is correct, she might not know. You decided to keep this question for later.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Anything else?

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The border matches the dry riverbed. It records <link="thirst">hunger and thirst</link> as her cause of death.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The symbol means a dry river. Check the actual riverbed or the records of lost water before we conclude that she died of hunger and thirst.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The wounds carried over when the other person woke. A mark on the shared body could carry a message between them.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The pictures match. But the medium is unknown.
(The hiss of the open line grows suddenly loud. Her answer returns without its usual firmness.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: No sign of anyone returning. She may have been the last. I used to think she would only notice me if I went missing too. I left. I never found out whether she did.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: One empty scan is not enough. Check the period after her burial.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: That is the altar infant. The figure is his <link="night_mother">mother in Night City</link>.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Compare the child with the altar infant. That will tell us who she was holding.
(She is quiet long enough for the static to return. When she speaks, she leaves no space between the short sentences.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: A flower. A mother and daughter drew it for each other when the girl was small. It meant "I love you." Just between them.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: It is not a blessing used throughout Night City. This one belonged to those two people.

else.speaker: Aurora
else.text: Show me the flower the searchlight recovered. We should not assume that every painted mark is a funerary symbol.

test_answer_repeated_beast.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_repeated_beast.text: On one stone, a creature might have belonged to a single life. When it keeps turning up on graves that have nothing else in common, I start to wonder what the whole city needed a way to say.

test_answer_repeated_beast.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_repeated_beast.text: Look for a pattern like that in Night City. If the same sign turns up on several graves there, ask yourself what those people kept leaving for one another. They may have had something quite different to say.

test_answer_repeated_blessing.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_repeated_blessing.text: The Crystal God, left as a shared blessing. It appears on graves of different people because it belongs to a custom, not to one person.

test_answer_repeated_blessing.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_repeated_blessing.text: The Nightfolk wish the departed well. The same sign, left again and again, makes that wish something the whole city can recognise.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The old account says the creature vanished in a single night. These little figures seem to carry that absence from stone to stone. They record <link="disappearance">disappearance</link>. You may find other traces of what disappearance meant for the Dayfolk.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: A familiar shape can travel from grave to grave without telling us its name. Look for the creature beyond these stones, #PLAYER#. Perhaps a trace of it—or the same icon returning again and again.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: This is an important step. Food went down; crystal came up. For a long while, each city worked to produce something the other needed. The stone has kept a little of that old dependence — though there is still insufficient evidence to establish whether they shared any aspect of life.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: I would be careful about asking a single stone to speak for two cities. We need some evidence that passed between them.

test_answer_scholar_20.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_scholar_20.text: I cannot speak for her. But I believe she must have discovered something about the world she lived in. Some truth she could not leave out of her own memorial. Your notebook is black and white for a reason, too.
(You look at your notebook once again. One double-page spread accommodating two contrasting halves. Does it signal a kind of coexistence, or a history of segregation?)

then.text: (The name of neither city comes easily. A tiny catch in her breathing survives the distance intact.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: A Dayfolk and a Nightfolk, hand in hand... I never expected her to be so cruel to herself.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: I cannot make out the picture, but I am fairly sure that fragment is skin — from past research, we know that the Dayfolk have blue blood, and some of it remains on the fragment. Try the searchlight. Take it back to a time before it decayed, before we decide what it was trying to say.

test_answer_scholar_31.text: (For a long while, only the thin electrical hum reaches you. Then a breath catches, and leaves her in a long, uneven sigh. You cannot see her, but for once the distance fails to conceal how much the question has touched her.)

test_answer_scholar_31.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_scholar_31.text: …or there is no one left to remember her. I made that decision. I made that decision...

test_answer_scholar_35.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_scholar_35.text: You are perceptive. Dayfolk and Nightfolk share one life. A wound left on one body is still there when the other wakes. Few people discovered they could send a message that way. Most called the injuries Nightfolk retaliation. The misunderstanding only widened the divide between the cities.

test_answer_scholar_39.text: (A small intake of breath. When she answers, the warmth has returned a little too neatly, like a blanket pulled over something that is still moving.)

test_answer_scholar_39.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_scholar_39.text: I imagine anyone would be moved, #PLAYER#. To make your own skin carry a message—well. We need not have known her to feel that. Shall we return to the investigation?

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: As the manuscript says, they gave her the title <link="scholar">Scholar</link> when she discovered what the crystal could do. Her stone remembers that work in the very material she studied—the work she was truly proud of.

(You can't help thinking back to the moment when you first saw the crystal in the Night City. Unlike its transparency in the Day City, the enigmatic darkness draws you in and makes you wonder how these beautiful stones changed Day and Night.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The crystal had a history before it became a memorial. #PLAYER#, find its mineral counterpart, or the record of the work it made possible.

test_answer_scholar_passage_gate.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_scholar_passage_gate.text: The gate was meant to close behind anyone going down. Its crystal power supply ran for far longer than it was designed to. The mechanism failed years ago, with the gate open. That’s how you’ve been able to cross in both directions.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: So many stones have borrowed the same creature. Its vanishing in the old account gives the carving its meaning: <link="disappearance">disappearance</link>. An image left behind where a life cannot be found.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: The creature keeps returning, doesn't it? Let us give it a name before we give it a meaning. What does the old account say?
(Perhaps use your tools to observe those markers again.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Yes. One unbroken base carries all three. They belong to the same family plot. The stone has kept them together, even after their stories parted.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: Look beneath their feet. A family resemblance may be written in the stone they stand on. Are their bases truly joined?

test_answer_sun_25.text: (Silence. Only the buzzing sound reminds you that the call is not interrupted.)

test_answer_sun_25.speaker: Aurora
test_answer_sun_25.text: Someone was still there after the others were gone. I wonder whether the family left a place for her, or whether she had already begun to leave it herself.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: ...I have nothing to tell.

else.text: (The answer comes before the question has quite left the channel. Then there is a silence just long enough for you to hear what slipped through.)

test_confrontation.text: (The wind echoes through the city no one has returned to. It might be your imagination, but it feels colder now.)
(You can't tell. We keep losing memories at every moment. Words said in the last moment, a warm smile that you pass by a minute ago, and those fleeting and private feelings attached to them.)
“We feel, and all that we have felt is swept away in the bright tumult of the world.”
(You first read Goethe's poem An Lottchen from Zweig's The World of Yesterday, where he recounts the beautiful world before the war that strips us of our humanity.)
(It is only when you witness a collapse that you realize how fragile our established routines can be. You wonder whether…)

items.label: The girl on the mark feels the same.
The Night girl in the diary feels the same.
Aurora feels the same.
What is the exact rule that governs disappearance and death across the cities?

body.speaker: Aurora
body.text: They have separate minds and take turns being awake. They share one living body. If one dies, the other cannot survive. What one city records as death, the other may record as disappearance.

items.label: Who are you?

body.text: (Her voice fractures, just like the world you are standing in, a world that belongs to yesterday.)

body.speaker: Aurora
body.text: I am someone who belongs to this place, yet something stops me from going back.

items.label: Return to the questions

then.speaker: #PLAYER#
then.text: You seem to know the link between disappearance and death, which proves the Scholar's speculation wrong. You know much more than I do. I want to know:

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: You saw that conflict — the Scholar ended up using skin as a medium to convey a message, proving her initial conclusion that the scars were caused by the Nightfolk wrong. This does not directly prove her conclusion about disappearance wrong, but I would encourage you to investigate along this thread.
(You can feel the strong implication behind her words. It feels like she knows everything but is still toying with you. You wonder if she will tell you where she's from and what she has done.)

else.speaker: Aurora
else.text: The Dayfolk often get stuck in their own understanding of the world. You may want to find more conflicts between the world they firmly believe in and the actual world around us.

test_ending_day_bear.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_bear.text: She left your toy at the marker you made before you escaped.

items.label: She was worried about you.
She came out to find you.
She loved you.
Despite the injustice she was complicit in.
Though you don't have to forgive her.
Though we all regret something that cannot be reversed.

test_ending_day_call.text: (You have your attribution with you. They mark your judgment after days of investigation.)
(Nothing right or wrong. It's all about interpretations.)
(But what each of us called right became, in all our hands, a wrong no one could undo.)

test_ending_day_call.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_call.text: Hi?
(A tentative greeting. As if it's the first time she's talking to you.)
(You may have captured a subtle sense of panic in her voice, as though that figure behind the husky voice is a lost teenage girl.)

test_ending_day_call.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_call.text: I have completed my investigation thoroughly.

test_ending_day_call.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_call.text: Good to hear. What else?

test_ending_day_call.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_call.text: I have to ask you a few questions… that might be personal.
(A brief, unnatural pause on the other side. You are not sure whether the person on the other side feels unprepared for the moment or has prepared for too long.)
(Long enough to be accustomed to waiting. Long enough to believe that this moment will never come.)

test_ending_day_call.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_call.text: Let me know your thoughts.

then.speaker: #PLAYER#
then.text: I've found the reason that the Twins collapsed. It's Night City does not have the concept of exchange.

then.speaker: #PLAYER#
then.text: I've found the reason that the Twins collapsed. It's The One-way Passage Order of the Day City.

then.speaker: #PLAYER#
then.text: I've found the reason that the Twins collapsed. It's Inducing effect of ONE being perceived as TWO.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: That's what I thought as well.

else.speaker: Aurora
else.text: Both of us know that it’s more than that.

test_ending_day_call.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_call.text: That's too similar to us human beings.

test_ending_day_call.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_call.text: We drew a line around ourselves and named it civilization.

test_ending_day_call.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_call.text: We expelled those beyond the defined boundaries and sent them downriver on a ship of fools.

test_ending_day_call.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_call.text: We watched it disappear, never knowing it carried our own flesh.
(She definitely knows what you are referring to. But you sense a more intimate implication beneath "flesh" as her word of choice.)

test_ending_day_call.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_call.text: Disappointment in your fellow man, I understand. What about your blood relatives?
(You also left them alone, with no intention of salvage. You didn't speak that out. They were teenage girls. You can't blame them for not saving the world that now remains in yesterday.)

test_ending_day_call.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_call.text: You knew it.

test_ending_day_dream.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_dream.text: It took me quite a while to understand "dream" in human language. Dayfolk viewed sleep as a rehearsal of death because we totally lose our consciousness when we fall asleep in the sleeping coffin. That's when our night counterparts fully deploy our life for the other part of a day.

test_ending_day_dream.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_dream.text: Then one day, after a day of conversation with the researchers, I was recalling the past details so intensely that I once again saw the familiar faces at night.

test_ending_day_dream.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_dream.text: It was the first time I witnessed how dark a long night can be, and the first time her appearance became so clear that I recognized her at first sight.

test_ending_day_dream.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_dream.text: She was younger than the woman I had in mind. The night was so dark that it blurred her look. But it's already the clearest out of that vast pool of memories across time.

test_ending_day_dream.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_dream.text: I said hi. Not sure if she responded. Perhaps deep in my consciousness I still had her voice, but I cannot frame it into a sound that I could match with her—the Scholar, or rather, my mother.

test_ending_day_dream.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_dream.text: She passed me the toy, smiling. She didn’t smile that much. She always looked worried. Day City is a place where everyone uses something to exchange for another, like my parents' marriage, like her education to me. That time she gave me a toy. First gift ever, not again.

test_ending_day_dream.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_dream.text: I woke up the next morning with tears on my cheeks. It's the first and last time that I understood what it means to have a dream.

test_ending_day_dream.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_dream.text: For years I've been anticipating another dream. Yet what I got were nights of complete silence. It was after the night I heard the whisper of the breeze on that remote star which I've never returned to that I felt the emptiness in that solitary silence.

items.label: You missed her.
You loved her.

test_ending_day_earth.text: (If things happened 50 years ago, you should now be speaking to an old lady that used to live on this planet.)

(A teenage girl thought that escaping would solve the entire problem. Yet when she's really light-years away from her homeland and dozens of years from the home in her memories, time suddenly becomes a counting unit that loses its tangibility.)
(The girl was stuck in the past that she was once determined to abandon.)

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_earth.text: I can't remember the day when the Earth first visited the Twins. I was found by the aliens. By then, I knew not a single word of human language, but I knew they wanted to pick us up.

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_earth.text: We were relying on food in the Day City and in the wild. Those days were more about surviving than living. I pointed to the sleeping coffin. They understood, and we were both fetched to Earth.

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_earth.text: Every day before my day ends, I write her a note on my thoughts and my progress in communicating with the people. Together, we learnt the human language.

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_earth.text: So you never did anything together?

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_earth.text: We can't. We are the closest friends that never met each other. That's the limitation the Twins were born with.

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_earth.text: The archaeologists were friendly to us. But "friendly" is a different word to "friend". To my shame, I started to miss the people that I once deemed as stubborn, harsh and cruel, and most importantly, hypocritical, the trait that I do not want myself to fall into the most.

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_earth.text: Neither of us can step out of the specially designed space adapted to our physical condition. Nothing is too different from our years of straying on the Twins.

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_earth.text: We were sharing the same flesh—not only the Day and the Night. Also my people and I. As they were lost, I'm lost, too.

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_earth.text: Have you ever been given a chance to come back?
(If they can travel that far to Earth and stay alive for years, they should be able to return. But they sent you as the delegate. There is a deeper reason that stopped her from looking back.)

test_ending_day_earth.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_earth.text: I always have the choice. The researchers ask us from time to time. It was me that did not want to look back.

items.label: Because your health cannot support a journey this long?
Because you are busy?
Because of your guilt?
But you don't have to look back.
You should allow yourself to preserve those emotions.
You might follow your heart to visit her again.
Even if she did not love you in the way you want.
Even if she is not perfect.
That's the complexity we have to embrace.

test_ending_day_goodbye.text: (You feel that tremor in your limbs again, with fear and a little bit of anticipation for her response.)
(For a while, she says nothing. You hear only the buzzing sound mixing with the wind.)
(The wind gets stronger. The night is about to come. Then you hear sobbing on the other side.)
(She hangs up without a goodbye. You keep the receiver to your ear. That beeping sound speaks for her struggles.)
(You sit until the moon rises, randomly thinking about your decisions if you were in their situation.)
(You suppose you know the answers. But as always, they remain assumptions that change nothing. You call again.)

items.label: Call again.

test_ending_day_guilt.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_day_guilt.text: You sent me here to make up for your guilt, but…

items.label: I can recover nothing but facts you mostly already know.
You have to face that by yourself.
A witness has no ability to resolve the knots for someone who experienced all this.

test_ending_day_return_1.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_return_1.text: To my surprise, I'm still quite healthy given my age and my living in a different environment.

test_ending_day_return_2.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_day_return_2.text: Time is the thing that I possess the most to waste.

test_ending_mothers_question.text: What did the mothers do to their daughter?

items.label: They simply love them.
They hurt them.
Hard to conclude, it's not black or white.

test_ending_night_childhood.text: (A long sigh comes from the other side.)

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: Nightfolk do not have a language. We have no order, no social construct, nothing other than digging for survival.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: We have icons. Some of them have a meaning that is agreed upon. Most of them remain between closely related individuals.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: We Nightfolk have bad eyesight. When I was a child, I put a flower discreetly on my mother's head. It was loosely tied to the ends of her hair. When she was back, the flower was still there. She never noticed it.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: I was laughing. She had a grin after me. The next day I put a flower in her hair again. Every day. Until one day I joined the working group and found that there was no way she could come back with that flower every day after that kind of rigorous labor.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: We never specifically define that icon. It's never painted, delivered as a letter, or conveyed like a wish that was featured on my brother's stone. It is a meaning that was never described.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: What I felt was only anger. I felt angry when my brother rested in her arms. I felt angry when she was standing on the altar and the group was singing the same hymn.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: I lost her when she became the godmother of our people. She no longer worked, and she took off the flower every day when she was preparing herself for the morning prayer.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: She decided to take off that unique icon just between us. The glossy son became her only child, a divine body that carried her flesh. I am nothing related to her.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: I thought escaping without her would free me from that attachment. I learnt language from Day City. I started to describe my feelings via the letters to the other Aurora, but I still could not describe my feelings towards my mother.

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_childhood.text: Until I reached the human world and encountered that word again as “love.”
(She stopped her narration with a breath of relief.)

test_ending_night_childhood.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_night_childhood.text: If so, are you coming back one day?
(No promise. No decision. But you opened up a possibility of returning home.)
(She said goodbye, and the radio never calls back.)

items.label: But no matter how I choose, my feelings do not prove your feelings to be wrong.
You don't need my answer to make yourself an individual worthy of others' empathy.

test_ending_night_escape.speaker: #PLAYER#
test_ending_night_escape.text: That hard decision was made when you were girls, definitely.

test_ending_night_escape.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_escape.text: Nothing hard for me. If I hadn't escaped, I would be locked in the underworld by the one-way passage.

items.label: But you had the choice to take your mother.
But you had an option to stay for your people.

test_ending_night_mother.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_mother.text: We've been talking for a while. You should know I don't care for someone who cares nothing about me.
(You spot slight reluctance towards the end of the sentence.)

then.speaker: #PLAYER#
then.text: I found a unique icon of a flower on your mother's stone, which repeats on your solitary marker. You told me that it is a symbol of love that is one of a kind, only between the two of you. Who left it there?
(Her voice is back to that sober tone, but with slight shivering hidden beneath.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: I left it there. My mother has never come to the ground since my brother's disappearance.

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: This doesn’t mean I love her. I just feel pity that no one else is going to understand its meaning after her. Let the stone remember it beyond my mother or myself.

then.speaker: #PLAYER#
then.text: She remembered that icon before her death. It was left on her tombstone.
(Silence. )

test_ending_night_mother.text: (Night Aurora drained herself to learn and survive. She had to pretend to be strong, to act as though none of the sacrifices had left a mark. Only then could she tell herself it had been worth leaving.)

items.label: It can still hurt. That doesn’t mean it wasn’t worth leaving.
Admitting love does not conflict with your need to escape.
You do not have to put yourself in opposition to your mom to justify your choice.

test_ending_night_note.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_note.text: She's more sensitive than I am. Oversensitive. The guilt is torturing her all the time. Poor…
(She swallowed the last word. A sudden realization that time passed.)

items.label: Poor Aurora.
Poor Girl.

test_ending_night_question.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_question.text: If you were me, how would you feel about my escape?

items.label: Honestly, I can never feel personally the ignorance you've been through, but I know it's tough.
You were not making the wrong choice. I might make similar choices.
It's a brave choice. We are born with attachments, which are so difficult to break.

test_ending_night_start.speaker: Aurora
test_ending_night_start.text: I read her note. I know what you are calling for.

items.label: Perhaps I know more than you thought.
But I still hope you can stay for the chat.

test_ending_reflect.text: (And they are one. One that shares the fate and memories of the civilization.)
(After some moments of solitude, you have to give Aurora a call. But before that, you might sort out your thoughts.)
What is the true reason of the civilization's fall?

items.label: Night City does not have the concept of exchange
The One-way Passage Order of the Day City
The effect of ONE being perceived as TWO

test_open_ending.text: (You are not sure if the Day Aurora will call back when the night ends. But you look to the horizon, and see a beautiful light shine from the back of the solitary stone.)
(No matter what—on Earth or these obsolete cities. Tomorrow the sun will rise.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: I didn't know she had the privilege of doing so, yet she never did. She was someone who valued reputation and recognition; she lived her life in the prescribed mold of a successful Dayfolk. But she never mentioned the mausoleum again. Why?
(The next line is so faint that it sounds like a whisper to herself.)

then.speaker: Aurora
then.text: She might be feeling as guilty as…
(The last few words disperse in the humming sound.)

else.speaker: Aurora
else.text: I'm not sure whether the Scholar is eligible… Have you found any evidence related to that?
